input.rationale: The previous end-to-end run produced the decisive raw values but its comparisons evaluated unknown because my harness contained two network tests emitting identically named events, so prerequisite association was ambiguous. This submission fixes that construction problem at its source: the harness now holds a single case, and its events are renamed uniquely (nonauto_setup, nonauto_probe, nonauto_apply) so each comparison has one unambiguous admission. The case is otherwise the same end-to-end flow: a real three-node network, the joint configuration entered and applied by every application with applied entries acknowledged so no conf change is pending unapplied, then the empty explicit-transition ConfChangeV2 proposed, shown in the log as an EntryConfChangeV2, committed, and applied. A local run records already_pending false, entry_type EntryConfChangeV2, committed_reached true and panicked true, so the comparisons should complete on the controller's receipt. No interpretation is added because that receipt does not exist yet.

scope.description: Single-case end-to-end demonstration with unambiguous event identities: a real three-node network with the application caught up, an empty explicit-transition ConfChangeV2 proposed, committed, and applied, recording the log entry type, whether the commit index reached it, and whether the apply panics.
assumptions: Real three-node raft network built with the package test helpers; leader 1 is elected by a MsgHup.

The joint configuration is entered by proposing and committing ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit, Changes: [add node 2, already a voter]} and having every application apply it, so no node outside the network is referenced.

Application progress is simulated by raftLog.appliedTo(committed) on each peer after the joint change commits, the effect of acknowledging applied entries through Advance, which clears the pending-conf guard.

The malformed change is ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit} with zero changes, proposed through raft.Step as an EntryConfChangeV2, and the entry is read back from the leader's log at the index it was appended to.
excluded: Any claim about client-side construction of change messages.
Configurations containing nodes absent from the network, which the test helper cannot represent; the earlier attempt that referenced such a node panicked inside the helper rather than in the library.

experiment.prefix: TestAssuranceCommittedNonAutoConfChange builds newNetwork(nil, nil, nil), elects leader 1 with a MsgHup, computes the index the joint change will occupy, and proposes ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit, Changes: [AddNode 2]} as an EntryConfChangeV2 through MsgProp. After delivery, every peer's application applies that change and acknowledges applied entries up to its commit index, and a setup event records state, joint flag, voters, outgoing voters, committed, applied, pendingConfIndex and alreadyPending. The test then computes the index the malformed change will occupy, proposes ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit} with zero changes, and emits a probe event with that index, the type of the entry read back from the log, the commit index and whether the commit index reached the entry. Finally it applies the malformed change inside a recover and emits whether it panicked, the panic text and whether the configuration is still joint.

comparisons.description: With the guard cleared, the malformed change is accepted and replicated as a configuration-change entry rather than rewritten to a normal entry.
That entry genuinely commits, so it reaches the application in the committed entries it must apply.
Applying the committed configuration-change entry panics, which is the documented action for a committed change the application does not reject.

knowledge.assertion: the pending-conf guard rewrites the entry to EntryNormal unless the application has acknowledged applied entries
with the application caught up the malformed change was kept as EntryConfChangeV2, committed at index 3 and panicked on apply

scope.description: Exercise the unexported readOnly confirmation path of package raft with ack values the live instance's heartbeatCtx never emitted, and record the two candidate consequences: an out-of-range slice in maybeAdvance, and confirmation of reads that the acking voter never observed.
assumptions: ack positions are supplied directly to readOnly.recvAck, standing in for MsgHeartbeatResp.Context values; this is an out-of-contract input, since the library's own follower path echoes the leader's context (see a167f4c33dc94f34b03ea29dbe7ec15a-knowledge-0).
ReadOnlySafe option; three voters (1,2,3) so the quorum position is the median of the stored acks.
The self-ack of the leader (id 1) is produced by heartbeatCtx() exactly as sendMsgReadIndexResponse does it.
excluded: Any claim that a legal cluster produces these inputs; the experiment characterises the code, not reachability.
Lease-based reads, which do not use the ack map.

basis.prefix: Each test builds a fresh readOnly via newReadOnly(ReadOnlySafe), admits one or two MsgReadIndex stand-ins through readOnly.addRequest(committedIndex, msg), self-acks with readOnly.recvAck(leaderID, readOnly.heartbeatCtx()), then injects peer acks with readOnly.recvAck(peerID, littleEndianUint64(position)) using values the leader never emitted, and finally calls readOnly.maybeAdvance(quorum.JointConfig with Voters[0]={1,2,3}). No raft instance, network or storage is involved; the ack map, unconfirmedReads and confirmedReads are read directly, and the maybeAdvance call in the oversized case is wrapped in a recover to record whether it panics.

comparisons.description: When the quorum ack position exceeds the number of outstanding read requests, maybeAdvance slices unconfirmedReads out of range and panics.
One forged ack value combined with the leader's self-ack reaches a 2-of-3 quorum position, so both admitted reads are confirmed although voter 3 never received a heartbeat carrying position 2.

knowledge.assertion: no in-model producer supplies a Context the live leader never emitted, which is why this experiment uses an out-of-contract input

experiments.revision_reason: The first version named both probe events read_ack_probe and both setup events read_ack_setup, so the controller correlated each comparison against the other case's prerequisite and returned unknown. This revision gives each case its own event names (read_oversized_setup/read_oversized_probe, read_forged_setup/read_forged_probe) so each comparison has a single, unambiguous admission. No target code, prefix, injected input or assertion changed.

scope.description: Drive a real raft leader that cannot obtain quorum acknowledgements and repeatedly submit ReadIndex with the same RequestCtx, measuring the queued read state and whether it survives being deposed.
assumptions: The node is a legitimate leader: newTestRaft with voters {1,2,3} in the storage ConfState, promoted via becomeCandidate/becomeLeader, with the library defaults (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe).

No MsgAppResp or MsgHeartbeatResp is delivered, which is the environment 'leader cannot obtain quorum acknowledgements'; outbound messages are cleared each round so growth is measured in raft state rather than in the msgs buffer.
Each round submits a fresh local MsgReadIndex with the same RequestCtx, which is the retry pattern the ReadIndex contract tells callers to perform.
excluded: Any claim about etcd's own retry policy or a particular caller's timer; only the library-side bound is measured.
Lease-based reads, which never enter the pending queue or ack structures.

basis.prefix: The test builds a real raft via newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it with becomeCandidate() then becomeLeader(), and emits a setup event recording state, term, committed, lastIndex, CheckQuorum, the read-only option and voter count. It then calls raft.Step 64 times with a local MsgReadIndex carrying the same RequestCtx, clearing r.msgs and r.msgsAfterAppend after each step, and emits the queue lengths. Finally it steps a higher-term MsgHeartbeat from node 2 to depose the leader and emits the queue lengths again to show whether the queued duty survives the authority transition.

comparisons.description: 64 same-context retries are all queued as separate pending read requests, matching the round count and showing no collapsing or bound.
After being deposed by a higher term, the node is a follower but the queued read requests are still retained, so the accumulation is not cancelled by the authority transition.

scope.description: Measure both admission outcomes of the ReadOnlySafe read path for a caller retrying ReadIndex with an identical RequestCtx: the queued path of a leader that has not committed in its term, and the admitted path of a leader that has committed in its term but whose follower stops acknowledging heartbeats.
assumptions: Both nodes are real raft instances built with the library defaults (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe); the queued case uses voters {1,2,3} and the admitted case {1,2}.

For the admitted case the leader's commit is produced the normal way - the leader's own MsgAppResp is stepped from msgsAfterAppend and then node 2 acknowledges the empty entry - so committedEntryInCurrentTerm() becomes true without any artificial state.

After that point no MsgHeartbeatResp is delivered, which is the environment 'followers stop acknowledging'; outbound messages are counted and then cleared each round so growth is measured in raft state and broadcasts are counted explicitly.
excluded: Any claim about a particular caller's retry timer, and any claim about lease-based reads.
Reads that are eventually confirmed: the point is what the leader accumulates while they are not.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceReadIndexPendingGrowth builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it, emits a setup event (state, term, committed, lastIndex, CheckQuorum, read-only option, voter count), steps 64 local MsgReadIndex messages with the same RequestCtx while clearing outbound traffic, emits the queue lengths, then steps a higher-term MsgHeartbeat from node 2 and emits the queue lengths again. TestAssuranceReadIndexAdmittedGrowth builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2))), promotes it, steps the self-ack messages out of msgsAfterAppend and then node 2's MsgAppResp for the empty entry so the leader commits in its term, emits a setup event including committedEntryInCurrentTerm(), then steps the same 64 same-context MsgReadIndex messages while counting MsgHeartbeat messages per round, and emits unconfirmedReads, broadcast count, pending length, confirmedReads and state.

comparisons.description: Queued path: 64 same-context retries are all retained as separate pending read requests.
Queued path: the accumulated requests survive deposition to StateFollower unchanged.
Admitted path: with the leader committed in its term but no heartbeat acknowledgements, 64 retries add 64 unconfirmed read requests.
Admitted path: each of the 64 retries also broadcasts one heartbeat, so retries cost outbound messages in addition to retained state.

knowledge.assertion: admission is per request and context-blind, and each admitted request broadcasts a heartbeat
the queued path accumulates one pending entry per retry and is not reclaimed by deposition

scope.description: Measure the drain burst: accumulate queued read requests on a leader that has not committed in its term, then let it commit in its term and record what the release path does with the whole queue in that one step.
assumptions: Real raft instance built with library defaults (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe) over voters {1,2}, so the leader becomes committed in its term once its own ack and node 2's MsgAppResp for the empty entry are delivered.
64 ReadIndex retries with an identical RequestCtx are submitted before any acknowledgement is delivered, so all of them take the queued path.

The commit is produced through the normal leadership path (self MsgAppResp stepped with From=1, then node 2's MsgAppResp at lastIndex), which is the call site that invokes releasePendingReadIndexMessages; the harness does not call the release function directly.
excluded: Any claim about a network schedule or about a caller's retry timer; only the step-local effect is measured.
Whether the released reads are then confirmed: no heartbeat response is delivered, so the re-admitted entries stay unconfirmed.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceReadIndexQueuedDrainBurst builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2))), promotes it with becomeCandidate/becomeLeader, clears the outbound buffers, submits 64 local MsgReadIndex messages with the same RequestCtx while clearing outbound traffic each round, and emits a setup event with the queue length, committed index, committedEntryInCurrentTerm() and unconfirmed length. It then steps a MsgAppResp with From=1 at lastIndex and node 2's MsgAppResp at lastIndex, which is the leader fast path that calls releasePendingReadIndexMessages, and emits the post-commit event with committed, in_term, queue length, unconfirmed length, the number of MsgHeartbeat messages produced in that step, and the node state.

comparisons.description: The single commit step empties the whole queued read set at once.
Every previously queued request is re-admitted into unconfirmedReads in that same step.
That one step emits one heartbeat per released request, so the retained queue also becomes a burst of outbound messages.

knowledge.assertion: releasePendingReadIndexMessages drains the queue through sendMsgReadIndexResponse, one response per queued message
the queued path accumulates one pending entry per retry

scope.description: Control for the growth claim: repeat the same-context ReadIndex retry pattern on a leader with CheckQuorum enabled, tick through an election timeout so the leader loses its quorum view, and record whether growth stops and whether the accumulated queue is reclaimed.
assumptions: Real raft instance built from newTestConfig with CheckQuorum set true over voters {1,2,3}, election timeout 3 ticks, ReadOnlySafe; no peer messages are delivered, so the quorum view is empty.
Retries are submitted in batches of eight between ticks (24 in total before the leader steps down), all with the same RequestCtx, which is the retry pattern the ReadIndex contract assigns to callers.
After the step-down eight more retries are submitted, so the harness also observes what a follower with no leader does with a read request.
excluded: Any claim that CheckQuorum is required or recommended for ReadOnlySafe; it is only used here as the competing liveness mechanism.
Any measurement of a network partition; the quorum view is emptied by delivering no messages.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceReadIndexGrowthWithCheckQuorum builds newTestConfig(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), sets CheckQuorum true, constructs the raft with newRaft, promotes it with becomeCandidate/becomeLeader and clears the outbound buffers. It emits a setup event (check_quorum, state, election timeout, voter count), then loops up to three ticks submitting eight same-context MsgReadIndex messages per tick while clearing outbound traffic, and emits a before event with the accumulated queue length, state and whether the window closed. It then submits eight more retries after the step-down and emits an after event with the queue length before and after, a boolean showing they are equal, the node state and the unconfirmed length.

comparisons.description: With CheckQuorum enabled the leader loses its quorum view within the election timeout, so the growth window does close on its own under that configuration.
Closing the window does not reclaim what was accumulated: further read requests after the step-down leave the queue at its previous length.

knowledge.assertion: the queued path accumulates one pending entry per retry and is not reclaimed by an authority transition

scope.description: Measure how much caller-supplied payload the leader retains when many distinct ReadIndex requests are accepted while it cannot obtain quorum acknowledgements, and verify that each retained payload is a distinct buffer rather than one shared slice counted repeatedly.
assumptions: Real raft over voters {1,2,3} built with newTestRaft (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe); no MsgAppResp or MsgHeartbeatResp is delivered, so every read takes the queued path.

64 requests are submitted, each carrying its own freshly allocated 4096-byte RequestCtx, modelling a caller issuing distinct reads (the ReadIndex API takes an opaque rctx []byte and documents no size limit).

Retention is summed over the Data fields of the entries held in pendingReadIndexMessages, and the number of distinct backing buffers is counted by taking the address of each buffer's first byte, so a shared slice would appear as distinct_ctx_buffers < pending.
excluded: Any claim about total process footprint (allocator overhead, per-message structs and slice headers are not counted) or about a specific deployment's memory limit.
Any claim that a caller must not send large contexts; only that the library accepts and retains whatever it is given.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceReadIndexRetainedBytes builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it with becomeCandidate/becomeLeader, clears the outbound buffers, and emits a setup event with CheckQuorum, state, voter count, the per-request context size and the round count. It then submits 64 MsgReadIndex messages, each with its own 4096-byte Data buffer, clearing outbound traffic each round, and finally emits a probe event with the pending queue length, the summed retained Data length, the number of distinct backing buffers and the node state.

comparisons.description: Every one of the 64 distinct read requests is retained.
The retained caller payload is 64 times 4096 bytes, i.e. the retry count multiplied by the caller-chosen context size.
The byte total is genuine retention: the 64 payloads sit in 64 distinct buffers, so the sum is not one shared slice counted repeatedly.

knowledge.assertion: the queued path retains one message per request and is not reclaimed

scope.description: Drive a real raft through entering a joint configuration and then through proposing and applying an empty ConfChangeV2 with an explicit transition, recording whether propose-time validation keeps the entry and whether applying it panics.
assumptions: Real raft over voters {1,2,3} built with newTestRaft and the library defaults; the joint configuration is entered by applying ConfChangeV2 with an explicit transition and a single add-node change, which is the normal EnterJoint path.

The malformed change is submitted through raft.Step as a MsgProp carrying an EntryConfChangeV2 built by marshalling ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit}, which is exactly the input shape an application or client would produce.

ApplyConfChange is invoked directly on the same instance because the entry would not be committed on a quorum-less test instance; no production logic is modified and the panic is captured with recover so it is recorded as data.
excluded: Any claim about how a client library or etcd constructs its ConfChangeV2 messages; only the library's own acceptance and apply paths are measured.
The Auto-transition empty change, which is the supported leave-joint idiom and is not part of this comparison.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceEmptyExplicitConfChangeJoint builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it with becomeCandidate/becomeLeader, applies ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit, Changes: [add 4]} and emits a setup event with the resulting voters, outgoing voters, the tested transition, change count, LeaveJoint and EnterJoint results. It then marshals ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit} into an EntryConfChangeV2, steps it as a MsgProp, and emits an event with the step error, how many entries were appended and the type of the last entry. Finally it calls applyConfChange on that same change inside a recover and emits whether it panicked, the panic text and whether the configuration is still joint.

comparisons.description: Propose-time validation kept the entry as a configuration change rather than replacing it, so the library accepted the request.
Applying the accepted change panics because Changer.EnterJoint rejects an already-joint configuration.

knowledge.assertion: the explicit-transition empty change passes validation and panics on apply

scope.description: Control for the empty-change-set panic finding: run the same joint configuration with an empty ConfChangeV2 that carries the documented Auto transition, and record that it leaves the joint configuration without panicking, next to the explicit-transition case that panics.
assumptions: Real raft over voters {1,2,3} built with newTestRaft and library defaults; the joint configuration is entered the same way in both cases (ConfChangeV2 with an explicit transition and one add-node change).
The control change is the zero-valued ConfChangeV2, which is the documented idiom for leaving a joint configuration.
ApplyConfChange is invoked directly in both cases because a quorum-less instance cannot commit; the panic is captured with recover so it is recorded as data, and no production logic is modified.
excluded: Any claim about client-side construction of change messages; only the two library forms are compared.
Cases where the configuration is not joint, which existing validation already rejects with a log message.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceEmptyAutoConfChangeLeavesJoint builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it, applies the same explicit-transition EnterJoint change as the other test, and emits a setup event with the configuration, the control change's transition, change count, LeaveJoint and EnterJoint results. It then applies the zero-valued ConfChangeV2 inside a recover and emits whether it panicked, the panic text, whether the configuration is still joint afterwards and the resulting voters. The other test in the same harness keeps the explicit-transition case, so one invocation records both the defect and its control.

comparisons.description: Control: the Auto-transition empty change does not panic, so the failure is specific to the explicit transition rather than to empty change sets.
Control: the Auto-transition empty change leaves the joint configuration as documented, showing the apply path works when the two leave-joint tests agree.

knowledge.assertion: validation derives leave-joint from len(Changes) == 0 while the apply path derives it from LeaveJoint, which also requires the Auto transition

scope.description: Cover both non-Auto transition values for the empty-change-set panic: the explicit transition already measured, the implicit transition added here, and the Auto control, all against the same joint configuration in one invocation.
assumptions: Real raft over voters {1,2,3} built with newTestRaft and library defaults; the joint configuration is entered identically in each case with ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit, Changes: [add 4]}.
The implicit case submits ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointImplicit} with zero changes through raft.Step as an EntryConfChangeV2, which is the same input shape as the explicit case.
ApplyConfChange is invoked directly in each case because a quorum-less instance cannot commit; the panic is captured with recover so it is recorded as data and no production logic is modified.
excluded: Any claim about client-side construction of change messages; only the library's transition values are compared.
Non-joint configurations, which validation already rejects with a log message and an entry rewrite.

basis.prefix: The harness now runs three cases over the same joint entry. TestAssuranceEmptyExplicitConfChangeJoint and TestAssuranceEmptyImplicitConfChangeJoint build newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promote it, apply the explicit-transition EnterJoint change, and emit a setup event naming the tested transition together with joint state, voters, voters_outgoing, change count, LeaveJoint and EnterJoint. Each then marshals its empty ConfChangeV2 into an EntryConfChangeV2, steps it as a MsgProp, emits the step error, appended count and last entry type, and finally applies that change inside a recover, emitting whether it panicked, the panic text and whether the configuration is still joint. TestAssuranceEmptyAutoConfChangeLeavesJoint is the control and emits the same shape with joint_after and voters_after.

comparisons.description: The implicit-transition empty change is also accepted by validation rather than replaced, so the trigger is not specific to JointExplicit.
The implicit-transition empty change panics on apply exactly like the explicit one, because EnterJoint accepts it as a joint transition while the configuration is already joint.

knowledge.assertion: the explicit-transition empty change passed validation and panicked on apply while the Auto form left the joint configuration without panicking
validation derives leave-joint from len(Changes) == 0 while the apply path derives it from LeaveJoint, which also requires the Auto transition

Configurations containing nodes absent from the network, which the test helper cannot represent.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceCommittedEmptyNonAutoConfChange builds newNetwork(nil, nil, nil), elects leader 1 with a MsgHup, records the index the joint change will occupy, and proposes ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit, Changes: [AddNode 2]} as an EntryConfChangeV2 through MsgProp. result.summary: Fixed at the source the construction problem that made the previous end-to-end receipt's comparisons unknown. The harness now contains a single case whose events have unique names (nonauto_setup, nonauto_probe, nonauto_apply), so each comparison has one unambiguous admission, and the case is the same end-to-end flow: a real three-node network, the joint configuration entered and applied by every application with applied entries acknowledged so no conf change is pending unapplied, then an empty explicit-transition ConfChangeV2 proposed, shown in the log as an EntryConfChangeV2, committed, and applied the way the API requires. The submission registers the experiment with a prerequisite on the cleared guard and three comparisons plus the two relevant facts as knowledge uses, so the controller's receipt should complete them; no interpretation is included because that receipt does not exist yet, and the earlier receipts, the asserted claim and its limitations are unchanged.

No raft instance, network or storage is involved; the ack map, unconfirmedReads and confirmedReads are read directly, and the maybeAdvance call in the oversized case is wrapped in a recover to record whether it panics.

One forged ack value combined with the leader's self-ack reaches a 2-of-3 quorum position, so both admitted reads are confirmed although voter 3 never received a heartbeat carrying position 2.

experiments.revision_reason: The first version named both probe events read_ack_probe and both setup events read_ack_setup, so the controller correlated each comparison against the other case's prerequisite and returned unknown. This revision gives each case its own event names (read_oversized_setup/read_oversized_probe, read_forged_setup/read_forged_probe) so each comparison has a single, unambiguous admission. No target code, prefix, injected input or assertion changed.

scope.description: Drive a real raft leader that cannot obtain quorum acknowledgements and repeatedly submit ReadIndex with the same RequestCtx, measuring the queued read state and whether it survives being deposed.
assumptions: The node is a legitimate leader: newTestRaft with voters {1,2,3} in the storage ConfState, promoted via becomeCandidate/becomeLeader, with the library defaults (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe).

No MsgAppResp or MsgHeartbeatResp is delivered, which is the environment 'leader cannot obtain quorum acknowledgements'; outbound messages are cleared each round so growth is measured in raft state rather than in the msgs buffer.
Each round submits a fresh local MsgReadIndex with the same RequestCtx, which is the retry pattern the ReadIndex contract tells callers to perform.
excluded: Any claim about etcd's own retry policy or a particular caller's timer; only the library-side bound is measured.
Lease-based reads, which never enter the pending queue or ack structures.

basis.prefix: The test builds a real raft via newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it with becomeCandidate() then becomeLeader(), and emits a setup event recording state, term, committed, lastIndex, CheckQuorum, the read-only option and voter count. It then calls raft.Step 64 times with a local MsgReadIndex carrying the same RequestCtx, clearing r.msgs and r.msgsAfterAppend after each step, and emits the queue lengths. Finally it steps a higher-term MsgHeartbeat from node 2 to depose the leader and emits the queue lengths again to show whether the queued duty survives the authority transition.

comparisons.description: 64 same-context retries are all queued as separate pending read requests, matching the round count and showing no collapsing or bound.
After being deposed by a higher term, the node is a follower but the queued read requests are still retained, so the accumulation is not cancelled by the authority transition.

scope.description: Measure both admission outcomes of the ReadOnlySafe read path for a caller retrying ReadIndex with an identical RequestCtx: the queued path of a leader that has not committed in its term, and the admitted path of a leader that has committed in its term but whose follower stops acknowledging heartbeats.
assumptions: Both nodes are real raft instances built with the library defaults (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe); the queued case uses voters {1,2,3} and the admitted case {1,2}.

For the admitted case the leader's commit is produced the normal way - the leader's own MsgAppResp is stepped from msgsAfterAppend and then node 2 acknowledges the empty entry - so committedEntryInCurrentTerm() becomes true without any artificial state.

After that point no MsgHeartbeatResp is delivered, which is the environment 'followers stop acknowledging'; outbound messages are counted and then cleared each round so growth is measured in raft state and broadcasts are counted explicitly.
excluded: Any claim about a particular caller's retry timer, and any claim about lease-based reads.
Reads that are eventually confirmed: the point is what the leader accumulates while they are not.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceReadIndexPendingGrowth builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it, emits a setup event (state, term, committed, lastIndex, CheckQuorum, read-only option, voter count), steps 64 local MsgReadIndex messages with the same RequestCtx while clearing outbound traffic, emits the queue lengths, then steps a higher-term MsgHeartbeat from node 2 and emits the queue lengths again. TestAssuranceReadIndexAdmittedGrowth builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2))), promotes it, steps the self-ack messages out of msgsAfterAppend and then node 2's MsgAppResp for the empty entry so the leader commits in its term, emits a setup event including committedEntryInCurrentTerm(), then steps the same 64 same-context MsgReadIndex messages while counting MsgHeartbeat messages per round, and emits unconfirmedReads, broadcast count, pending length, confirmedReads and state.

comparisons.description: Queued path: 64 same-context retries are all retained as separate pending read requests.
Queued path: the accumulated requests survive deposition to StateFollower unchanged.
Admitted path: with the leader committed in its term but no heartbeat acknowledgements, 64 retries add 64 unconfirmed read requests.
Admitted path: each of the 64 retries also broadcasts one heartbeat, so retries cost outbound messages in addition to retained state.

knowledge.assertion: admission is per request and context-blind, and each admitted request broadcasts a heartbeat
the queued path accumulates one pending entry per retry and is not reclaimed by deposition

scope.description: Measure the drain burst: accumulate queued read requests on a leader that has not committed in its term, then let it commit in its term and record what the release path does with the whole queue in that one step.
assumptions: Real raft instance built with library defaults (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe) over voters {1,2}, so the leader becomes committed in its term once its own ack and node 2's MsgAppResp for the empty entry are delivered.
64 ReadIndex retries with an identical RequestCtx are submitted before any acknowledgement is delivered, so all of them take the queued path.

The commit is produced through the normal leadership path (self MsgAppResp stepped with From=1, then node 2's MsgAppResp at lastIndex), which is the call site that invokes releasePendingReadIndexMessages; the harness does not call the release function directly.
excluded: Any claim about a network schedule or about a caller's retry timer; only the step-local effect is measured.
Whether the released reads are then confirmed: no heartbeat response is delivered, so the re-admitted entries stay unconfirmed.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceReadIndexQueuedDrainBurst builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2))), promotes it with becomeCandidate/becomeLeader, clears the outbound buffers, submits 64 local MsgReadIndex messages with the same RequestCtx while clearing outbound traffic each round, and emits a setup event with the queue length, committed index, committedEntryInCurrentTerm() and unconfirmed length. It then steps a MsgAppResp with From=1 at lastIndex and node 2's MsgAppResp at lastIndex, which is the leader fast path that calls releasePendingReadIndexMessages, and emits the post-commit event with committed, in_term, queue length, unconfirmed length, the number of MsgHeartbeat messages produced in that step, and the node state.

comparisons.description: The single commit step empties the whole queued read set at once.
Every previously queued request is re-admitted into unconfirmedReads in that same step.
That one step emits one heartbeat per released request, so the retained queue also becomes a burst of outbound messages.

knowledge.assertion: releasePendingReadIndexMessages drains the queue through sendMsgReadIndexResponse, one response per queued message
the queued path accumulates one pending entry per retry

scope.description: Control for the growth claim: repeat the same-context ReadIndex retry pattern on a leader with CheckQuorum enabled, tick through an election timeout so the leader loses its quorum view, and record whether growth stops and whether the accumulated queue is reclaimed.
assumptions: Real raft instance built from newTestConfig with CheckQuorum set true over voters {1,2,3}, election timeout 3 ticks, ReadOnlySafe; no peer messages are delivered, so the quorum view is empty.
Retries are submitted in batches of eight between ticks (24 in total before the leader steps down), all with the same RequestCtx, which is the retry pattern the ReadIndex contract assigns to callers.
After the step-down eight more retries are submitted, so the harness also observes what a follower with no leader does with a read request.
excluded: Any claim that CheckQuorum is required or recommended for ReadOnlySafe; it is only used here as the competing liveness mechanism.
Any measurement of a network partition; the quorum view is emptied by delivering no messages.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceReadIndexGrowthWithCheckQuorum builds newTestConfig(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), sets CheckQuorum true, constructs the raft with newRaft, promotes it with becomeCandidate/becomeLeader and clears the outbound buffers. It emits a setup event (check_quorum, state, election timeout, voter count), then loops up to three ticks submitting eight same-context MsgReadIndex messages per tick while clearing outbound traffic, and emits a before event with the accumulated queue length, state and whether the window closed. It then submits eight more retries after the step-down and emits an after event with the queue length before and after, a boolean showing they are equal, the node state and the unconfirmed length.

comparisons.description: With CheckQuorum enabled the leader loses its quorum view within the election timeout, so the growth window does close on its own under that configuration.
Closing the window does not reclaim what was accumulated: further read requests after the step-down leave the queue at its previous length.

knowledge.assertion: the queued path accumulates one pending entry per retry and is not reclaimed by an authority transition

scope.description: Measure how much caller-supplied payload the leader retains when many distinct ReadIndex requests are accepted while it cannot obtain quorum acknowledgements, and verify that each retained payload is a distinct buffer rather than one shared slice counted repeatedly.
assumptions: Real raft over voters {1,2,3} built with newTestRaft (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe); no MsgAppResp or MsgHeartbeatResp is delivered, so every read takes the queued path.

64 requests are submitted, each carrying its own freshly allocated 4096-byte RequestCtx, modelling a caller issuing distinct reads (the ReadIndex API takes an opaque rctx []byte and documents no size limit).

Retention is summed over the Data fields of the entries held in pendingReadIndexMessages, and the number of distinct backing buffers is counted by taking the address of each buffer's first byte, so a shared slice would appear as distinct_ctx_buffers < pending.
excluded: Any claim about total process footprint (allocator overhead, per-message structs and slice headers are not counted) or about a specific deployment's memory limit.
Any claim that a caller must not send large contexts; only that the library accepts and retains whatever it is given.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceReadIndexRetainedBytes builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it with becomeCandidate/becomeLeader, clears the outbound buffers, and emits a setup event with CheckQuorum, state, voter count, the per-request context size and the round count. It then submits 64 MsgReadIndex messages, each with its own 4096-byte Data buffer, clearing outbound traffic each round, and finally emits a probe event with the pending queue length, the summed retained Data length, the number of distinct backing buffers and the node state.

comparisons.description: Every one of the 64 distinct read requests is retained.
The retained caller payload is 64 times 4096 bytes, i.e. the retry count multiplied by the caller-chosen context size.
The byte total is genuine retention: the 64 payloads sit in 64 distinct buffers, so the sum is not one shared slice counted repeatedly.

knowledge.assertion: the queued path retains one message per request and is not reclaimed

scope.description: Drive a real raft through entering a joint configuration and then through proposing and applying an empty ConfChangeV2 with an explicit transition, recording whether propose-time validation keeps the entry and whether applying it panics.
assumptions: Real raft over voters {1,2,3} built with newTestRaft and the library defaults; the joint configuration is entered by applying ConfChangeV2 with an explicit transition and a single add-node change, which is the normal EnterJoint path.

The malformed change is submitted through raft.Step as a MsgProp carrying an EntryConfChangeV2 built by marshalling ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit}, which is exactly the input shape an application or client would produce.

ApplyConfChange is invoked directly on the same instance because the entry would not be committed on a quorum-less test instance; no production logic is modified and the panic is captured with recover so it is recorded as data.
excluded: Any claim about how a client library or etcd constructs its ConfChangeV2 messages; only the library's own acceptance and apply paths are measured.
The Auto-transition empty change, which is the supported leave-joint idiom and is not part of this comparison.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceEmptyExplicitConfChangeJoint builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it with becomeCandidate/becomeLeader, applies ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit, Changes: [add 4]} and emits a setup event with the resulting voters, outgoing voters, the tested transition, change count, LeaveJoint and EnterJoint results. It then marshals ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit} into an EntryConfChangeV2, steps it as a MsgProp, and emits an event with the step error, how many entries were appended and the type of the last entry. Finally it calls applyConfChange on that same change inside a recover and emits whether it panicked, the panic text and whether the configuration is still joint.

comparisons.description: Propose-time validation kept the entry as a configuration change rather than replacing it, so the library accepted the request.
Applying the accepted change panics because Changer.EnterJoint rejects an already-joint configuration.

knowledge.assertion: the explicit-transition empty change passes validation and panics on apply

scope.description: Control for the empty-change-set panic finding: run the same joint configuration with an empty ConfChangeV2 that carries the documented Auto transition, and record that it leaves the joint configuration without panicking, next to the explicit-transition case that panics.
assumptions: Real raft over voters {1,2,3} built with newTestRaft and library defaults; the joint configuration is entered the same way in both cases (ConfChangeV2 with an explicit transition and one add-node change).
The control change is the zero-valued ConfChangeV2, which is the documented idiom for leaving a joint configuration.
ApplyConfChange is invoked directly in both cases because a quorum-less instance cannot commit; the panic is captured with recover so it is recorded as data, and no production logic is modified.
excluded: Any claim about client-side construction of change messages; only the two library forms are compared.
Cases where the configuration is not joint, which existing validation already rejects with a log message.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceEmptyAutoConfChangeLeavesJoint builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it, applies the same explicit-transition EnterJoint change as the other test, and emits a setup event with the configuration, the control change's transition, change count, LeaveJoint and EnterJoint results. It then applies the zero-valued ConfChangeV2 inside a recover and emits whether it panicked, the panic text, whether the configuration is still joint afterwards and the resulting voters. The other test in the same harness keeps the explicit-transition case, so one invocation records both the defect and its control.

comparisons.description: Control: the Auto-transition empty change does not panic, so the failure is specific to the explicit transition rather than to empty change sets.
Control: the Auto-transition empty change leaves the joint configuration as documented, showing the apply path works when the two leave-joint tests agree.

knowledge.assertion: validation derives leave-joint from len(Changes) == 0 while the apply path derives it from LeaveJoint, which also requires the Auto transition

scope.description: Cover both non-Auto transition values for the empty-change-set panic: the explicit transition already measured, the implicit transition added here, and the Auto control, all against the same joint configuration in one invocation.
assumptions: Real raft over voters {1,2,3} built with newTestRaft and library defaults; the joint configuration is entered identically in each case with ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit, Changes: [add 4]}.
The implicit case submits ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointImplicit} with zero changes through raft.Step as an EntryConfChangeV2, which is the same input shape as the explicit case.
ApplyConfChange is invoked directly in each case because a quorum-less instance cannot commit; the panic is captured with recover so it is recorded as data and no production logic is modified.
excluded: Any claim about client-side construction of change messages; only the library's transition values are compared.
Non-joint configurations, which validation already rejects with a log message and an entry rewrite.

basis.prefix: The harness now runs three cases over the same joint entry. TestAssuranceEmptyExplicitConfChangeJoint and TestAssuranceEmptyImplicitConfChangeJoint build newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promote it, apply the explicit-transition EnterJoint change, and emit a setup event naming the tested transition together with joint state, voters, voters_outgoing, change count, LeaveJoint and EnterJoint. Each then marshals its empty ConfChangeV2 into an EntryConfChangeV2, steps it as a MsgProp, emits the step error, appended count and last entry type, and finally applies that change inside a recover, emitting whether it panicked, the panic text and whether the configuration is still joint. TestAssuranceEmptyAutoConfChangeLeavesJoint is the control and emits the same shape with joint_after and voters_after.

comparisons.description: The implicit-transition empty change is also accepted by validation rather than replaced, so the trigger is not specific to JointExplicit.
The implicit-transition empty change panics on apply exactly like the explicit one, because EnterJoint accepts it as a joint transition while the configuration is already joint.

knowledge.assertion: the explicit-transition empty change passed validation and panicked on apply while the Auto form left the joint configuration without panicking
validation derives leave-joint from len(Changes) == 0 while the apply path derives it from LeaveJoint, which also requires the Auto transition

scope.description: End-to-end demonstration on a real three-node network: with the application caught up (no conf change pending unapplied), propose an empty ConfChangeV2 whose transition is explicit, show the entry is accepted as a configuration change and commits, and show that applying the committed entry panics.
assumptions: Real three-node raft network built with the package test helpers; leader 1 is elected by a MsgHup.

The joint configuration is entered by proposing and committing ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit, Changes: [add node 2, already a voter]} and having every application apply it, so the joint config is {1,2,3} against {1,2,3} and no node outside the network is referenced.

Application progress is simulated by calling raftLog.appliedTo(committed) on each peer after the joint change commits, which is the effect of acknowledging applied entries through Advance; this clears the pending-conf guard.

The malformed change is proposed through raft.Step as an EntryConfChangeV2 carrying ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit} with zero changes, and the entry is read back from the leader's log at the index it was appended to.
excluded: Any claim about client-side construction of change messages; the library's acceptance, replication and apply paths are what is measured.
Configurations containing nodes absent from the network, which the test helper cannot represent.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceCommittedEmptyNonAutoConfChange builds newNetwork(nil, nil, nil), elects leader 1 with a MsgHup, records the index the joint change will occupy, and proposes ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit, Changes: [AddNode 2]} as an EntryConfChangeV2 through MsgProp. Once the network has delivered it, every peer's application applies that change and acknowledges applied entries up to its commit index, and a setup event records joint state, voters, outgoing voters, committed, applied, pendingConfIndex and alreadyPending. The test then records the index the malformed change will occupy, proposes ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit} with zero changes, and emits a probe event with that index, the type of the entry actually in the log, the commit index and whether the commit index reached the entry. Finally it applies the malformed change inside a recover and emits whether it panicked, the panic text and whether the configuration is still joint.

comparisons.description: With the guard cleared, the malformed change is accepted and replicated as a configuration-change entry rather than rewritten.
That entry genuinely commits, so an application would see it in the committed entries it is required to apply.
Applying the committed configuration-change entry panics, which is the documented application action for a committed change it does not reject.

knowledge.assertion: the pending-conf guard rewrites the entry to EntryNormal unless the application has acknowledged applied entries
with the guard inactive the explicit-transition empty change stayed an EntryConfChangeV2 and panicked on apply

scope.description: Single-case end-to-end demonstration with unambiguous event identities: a real three-node network with the application caught up, an empty explicit-transition ConfChangeV2 proposed, committed, and applied, recording the log entry type, whether the commit index reached it, and whether the apply panics.
assumptions: Real three-node raft network built with the package test helpers; leader 1 is elected by a MsgHup.

The joint configuration is entered by proposing and committing ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit, Changes: [add node 2, already a voter]} and having every application apply it, so no node outside the network is referenced.

Application progress is simulated by raftLog.appliedTo(committed) on each peer after the joint change commits, the effect of acknowledging applied entries through Advance, which clears the pending-conf guard.

The malformed change is ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit} with zero changes, proposed through raft.Step as an EntryConfChangeV2, and the entry is read back from the leader's log at the index it was appended to.
excluded: Any claim about client-side construction of change messages.
Configurations containing nodes absent from the network, which the test helper cannot represent; the earlier attempt that referenced such a node panicked inside the helper rather than in the library.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceCommittedNonAutoConfChange builds newNetwork(nil, nil, nil), elects leader 1 with a MsgHup, computes the index the joint change will occupy, and proposes ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit, Changes: [AddNode 2]} as an EntryConfChangeV2 through MsgProp. After delivery, every peer's application applies that change and acknowledges applied entries up to its commit index, and a setup event records state, joint flag, voters, outgoing voters, committed, applied, pendingConfIndex and alreadyPending. The test then computes the index the malformed change will occupy, proposes ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit} with zero changes, and emits a probe event with that index, the type of the entry read back from the log, the commit index and whether the commit index reached the entry. Finally it applies the malformed change inside a recover and emits whether it panicked, the panic text and whether the configuration is still joint.

comparisons.description: With the guard cleared, the malformed change is accepted and replicated as a configuration-change entry rather than rewritten to a normal entry.
That entry genuinely commits, so it reaches the application in the committed entries it must apply.
Applying the committed configuration-change entry panics, which is the documented action for a committed change the application does not reject.

knowledge.assertion: the pending-conf guard rewrites the entry to EntryNormal unless the application has acknowledged applied entries
with the application caught up the malformed change was kept as EntryConfChangeV2, committed at index 3 and panicked on apply
